title: What If Lightning Struck You? Nine in Ten Survive

scenes.text: What if lightning hit you? Nine out of ten people survive.
The odds of being struck in a year are about one in one point two million, according to NOAA.
The bolt heats the air around it to about fifty thousand degrees Fahrenheit, over forty thousand hotter than the surface of the Sun.
It can burn skin, sometimes leaving branching marks called Lichtenberg figures, and disrupt the heart and nervous system.
Most deaths come from cardiac arrest at the moment of the strike. Others die days later from brain damage.
Still, roughly two hundred and forty thousand people survive strikes each year, though many are left with some disability.
